_purpose: GOAT calibration corpus (ko). Hand-authored expectations for the WHOLE pipeline: classify() intent + parse() slots. Seeded from .superpowers/research/ko-expressions.md (575 rows, incl. its parser-trap appendix G), crossed systematically over {amount form} x {pay verb} x {josa} x {split form} x {noise}, and extended with every sentence this branch's review rounds argued about (docs/SOLVED.md + the SDD ledger).
_howToRead: payer/participants name members; 'actor' is the person typing. A row with a `known` field is a PINNED MISS: `expect` records today's behavior and `known` says why it is not fixed. Never weaken a row to make it pass — fix the parser, or pin it with a justification.

rows.known: 오천 is a mined NUMBER_DECOY (a real word/place name), and the T3 ruling is that only a CURRENCY word rescues a decoy reading — 오천원 커피 reads 5000 correctly, and 5천 커피 does too. Bare 오천 with no currency word therefore stays null: a miss, but in the safe direction, and reversing the ruling would re-open the 천사/만일 class the decoy list exists for.

rows.known: Recall gap carried from T6: 오만 collides with a mined decoy and nothing rescues it across the space, so the whole phrase reads null instead of 55000. Null is the SAFE direction and strictly better than the pre-T6 behaviour, which reported a confidently wrong 5000 — fixing it needs the cross-token decoy rescue that T3 ruled out of scope.

rows.note: A bare 4-digit number IS money in Korean chat (숙소 120000, 커피 4500) — the parser cannot tell this from an app handle, and does not try. It reads it at 0.6 confidence as an UNMARKED hit, which is exactly why index.ts prefers a MARKED mention over a bare one; the confirm card is what catches the rest.

rows.known: The reader consumes 오천이 as 5002 and endsOnUnconfirmedDigit (T6) rejects the whole read rather than trusting a trailing Sino digit no currency word confirms. 5000 would be the right answer, but the alternative the guard prevents is BOOKING 5002 — a confidently wrong number — so null stands. 오천원이 나왔어 reads 5000 correctly.

rows.known: -아/어내다 compounds (지내다/견뎌내다) CONTAIN the pay stem 냈, so the sentence carries an expense signal and P5 opens an ASK-AMOUNT card. No amount is invented and no payer is stolen — the cost is one unnecessary "how much?" and a syllable eaten out of the description. Killing it needs either a full ending-consumption grammar for every pay stem or a compound-verb lexicon, both of which are larger than calibration and risk silencing real glued forms (밥값냈어). Documented at T7 fix round 1 and re-confirmed by the 1,000-row Korean fuzz sample, where this class produces ZERO amounts and ZERO wrong payers.

rows.known: The 보낸-guard is narrower than "보내다 is never a payment": it asks whether the WHOLE token is another verb's CLAUSE form, and ko/attributive.ts reads attributive/connective forms (보낸/보내는/보내고) but not finite pasts (보냈어). So 냈 still fires inside 보냈어 — 유나 is credited as payer (defensible: 송금 IS a payment in this domain, which is why T7 documented the family as benign) but the description is left holding the stranded 보. Closing it needs a past-tense rule in the clause reader, which is more than the mandated row asked for. The comment on the guard in parsers/split.ts states this scope explicitly.

rows.known: DOCUMENTED LOSS, deliberately traded: an `ambiguous` stem matches only where its token starts, so a noun glued in front of 내고 hides it and no pay verb is reported. This is the pre-branch behaviour restored (the bare 내 stem did not exist before Task 11), and it is what buys silence on the 17 start-of-word and inside-word collisions the mecab sweep found — 안내자, 안내대, 끝내지, 끝내어, 티내네, 제내지, 방송내보내다니 and the 내게/내음/내구 family. Unambiguous stems are untouched: 밥값냈어 still reports its verb and its payer.
